name: trips
description: Use when the symptom shows up while driving, or you need how the engine behaved over a recorded drive (warm-up, max coolant, rpm, boost).
instructions: Call list_trips {} first: it lists this car's recorded trips, newest first, with id, start time, minutes, km, max coolant, max rpm and average L/100 km.
Call read_trip with an id from that list, e.g. {"id":"1732350000000"}, for per-PID min / avg / max; add pids to look at other logged values, e.g. {"id":"…","pids":["0110","015E"]}.
To judge the cooling system, call read_trip {"id":"latest_cold"}: it picks the newest trip that started with coolant at or under 40 °C and reports the warm-up minutes.
Trips are what the user recorded on this phone for this car only. When list_trips says none are recorded, ask the user to record a drive in Trip recording rather than guessing.
interpret: Warm-up from a cold start (≤ 40 °C) to 80 °C: about 5-15 min of normal driving on most engines, longer on a diesel at idle or in winter. Over 20 min of driving, or a trip that never reaches 80 °C, points to a thermostat stuck open.
"started warm" means the engine was already warm at the start: that trip says nothing about the warm-up.
Max coolant over 110 °C on a trip points to overheating under load (coolant level, fan, water pump, radiator).
Distance comes from the speed PID (010D); "distance n/a" means speed was not logged. "no fuel data" means the trip logged neither fuel rate (015E) nor MAF (0110).
A trip's max rpm and MAP (010B) show how hard it was driven: compare like with like before calling one trip worse than another.
